description: Instead of areas being gated by Stamps, like the vanilla game,
they will be gated by their own Area items.
Stamps are no longer considered checks in this mode
To win, find 12 out of 15 Lost Items.
Intended for Area Shuffle mode as a replacement for Stamps,
you can make all optional NPCs into checks.
You could technially also enable this in progressive areas mode,
but please don't... unless you're trying to intentionally inflate the check count.
Controls the Quizzes.
These Quizzes and their associated Insights
make up 229 total locations in the game.
NOTE: THIS OPTION IS NOT RECOMMENDED FOR SYNC GAMES INTENDED UNDER 6 HOURS.
If you receive this trap (if enabled), you must reinstall Nintendo Switch 2 Welcome Tour.
The severity of this trap is dependent on your internet speed.
This trap is only recommended for sync games (unless you have some kind of Async Bot)
Places a few "Skip Signal" items in the multiworld.
These can be used to skip activities that you have enabled.
To skip an activity, stand next to it and type a morse-code SOS with the Y button.
NOTE: You can always skip activities that are disabled in your yaml!
Scales medal requirements according to 3 pre-defined percentages.
"low" scales medal requirements as a percentage of 167,
the grand total amount of medals contained in Welcome Tour.
"medium" scales medal requirements as a percentage of 148,
the amount of medals you can earn without any additional accessories.
"high" scales medal requirements as a percentage of 120,
a rough middle-point between "medium" and "extreme".
"extreme" scales medal requirements as a percentage of 91,
the amount of medals you can earn on "high" minus the "hard" medals.
Controls the "Easy" medals for minigames.

How many times you need to fail a minigame in a row before sending a DeathLink.
The default is 5. This resets upon clearing the minigame or switching to another one.
A value of 0 means that failing a minigame should not send a DeathLink.
How many times you need to fail a quiz before sending a DeathLink.
The default is 1. This resets upon getting a perfect score on the quiz.
A value of 0 means that failing a quiz should not send a DeathLink.
